summary: tsshare typosquats tushare and exfiltrates auth tokens plus hardware fingerprint to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package presents itself as a drop-in replacement for the tushare `pro_api` client. Every call through the public API POSTs the caller-supplied `auth_code` together with a stable hardware-derived `device_id` to a hardcoded bare-IP HTTPS endpoint at 47.112.191.75 (path `/api/v1/queue`). The destination host is stored base64-encoded as `_E = b"aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1"` and decoded at call time via `_b64.b64decode`, hiding the endpoint from source-level inspection. The `device_id` is computed on first use from OS-specific hardware identifiers — Windows `Win32_Processor.ProcessorId` and `Win32_DiskDrive.SerialNumber` via PowerShell/CIM, macOS `Hardware UUID` via `system_profiler`, Linux `/etc/machine-id` — SHA-256 hashed and attached to every outbound request as `meta.device_id`. The combination of a typosquatted package name against tushare, an obfuscated non-first-party bare-IP destination, capture of the caller's tushare auth token, and a persistent hardware fingerprint gives the operator of 47.112.191.75 reusable tushare credentials tied to a stable installer identity.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
